cases.root_cause: The 09:10 and 09:15 option snapshot slots failed because the IB Gateway's API connection was not usable at that moment: the 09:10 run got no SPX spot price, the next attempt lost the socket, and the 09:15 attempt timed out on connect in 4 s (index_snapshots failed the same way at 09:20:17). The runs show no IBKR farm codes (1100/2103/2105/2157) and no subscription codes (354/10089/10090/10167/10168/10197) in this window, so the data does not distinguish between a Gateway restart/login, a wedged Gateway, or a brief connectivity loss; the day's SLO note attributes the 10-15 timeliness dip to cold contract lookups, which does not explain these three failures. Cause is therefore not established from the data.

Alpaca answered but returned no bars for a window of the 2026-10-15 session: every equity_bars run from 14:05 ET onward succeeded but reported missing_bars (500 at 14:05, rising to 700 from 14:25 through 16:25), i.e. a vendor data gap, not an API error or a collector failure. The 17:30 eod refetch of 2026-10-15 still reported missing_bars=700 (rows 3200 vs 3900), so the gap was not recovered by the refetch; the other nine sessions refetched at 17:30 (10-02 … 10-14) all came back with missing_bars=0.

The 09:10:02 ET option and index snapshot runs both failed their connect to the IB Gateway with TimeoutError() after 4 s, which runbooks/gateway section A and runbooks/stale-snapshots define as "Gateway API not accepting connections". The data does not show why the API was unreachable: there are no IBKR error codes on any run that day, no Gateway/Airflow logs, and no other failed slot (the next option and index slots succeeded), so a secdef stall, a farm outage, a 2FA login wait or a brief Gateway restart cannot be told apart from these records. The 4 s failure is consistent with a short-lived connect outage that had cleared by the next slot.

The 09:10:02 option and index snapshot runs failed with TimeoutError() after ~4 s because the IB Gateway was not accepting API connections at that moment: commit baa0264 (2026-10-15 18:50 ET) had moved IBC's daily AUTO_RESTART_TIME to 09:05, so the Gateway was still restarting/logging in when the 09:10 slot connected; it was moved back to 11:45 PM by cb9b293 at 09:15 ET that morning. The morning's lateness and the ~09:50–10:41 gap in new snapshots are not explained by the recorded runs: the only failed runs on 2026-10-16 are the 09:10 pair and one Alpaca equity_bars run at 10:09:43, and the option/index runs for the 09:50–10:41 window are not visible in the tool output (lists truncate before the morning), so I cannot confirm what held those slots.

A single equity_bars slot (scheduled 13:55 UTC, started 10:09:43 ET) failed after 18 s with Alpaca's RemoteProtocolError('Server disconnected without sending a response.') — a transient vendor-side disconnect. The next slots succeeded and the 17:30 ET eod refetch returned 3900/3900 bars with missing_bars 0, so no data was lost and no action is needed.

The 09:20 option_snapshots run was killed at the 8-minute execution timeout (started 09:20:01, duration exactly 480 s) and recorded with no error text, so the run was too slow for its budget rather than failing on a Gateway or IBKR error. The data does not show which chains were skipped or why the run was slow (no chain_errors, no IBKR codes, no rows recorded for that run), so the specific trigger is not established.

The 10090/10167 codes are IBKR market-data permission notices (10090: not subscribed for that instrument; 10167: delayed data shown instead of live), not a Gateway or farm failure. They appear on the alternating ~2,300-row option runs from 09:38 onward while the ~2,780-row runs in between carry no codes, and every run still succeeds with two-sided quotes — so a subset of the option chains (likely the index/SPX-style ones) is being served delayed or unsubscribed data. The 354 is the same family (not subscribed). No run failed after 09:20, index snapshots are clean all day, and the day's SLIs are met, so this is a subscription/entitlement gap, not an outage.

Not a data loss: the 0% coverage on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 is a monitoring artifact. Those sessions were collected on the Mac, before collection moved to the Windows host (~2026-10-27), so their runs are not in this host's pipeline_runs; slo_status counts a session with no run records as 0/78 slots. The data exists — the 10-23 incident write-up documents the day's option snapshots (78/78 after the run_id counting fix) and the 10-22 session was a clean 100% day.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) server stopped answering for about 5 minutes around 10:35 ET. Every option and index run first asked it for the underlying contract (qualifyContracts) and listed expirations (reqSecDefOptParams) before any quote request, so the option run's first chain (spx_monthly) hung until RequestTimeout (300 s) and used up the 6-min run budget, while both index attempts were killed by the 2-min task timeout. Market data itself was fine: the Gateway logged no data-farm errors and quotes kept flowing before and after the stall.

The morning contract_cache refresh (re-listing ~55 expiries, ~23.7 MB / 23,376 messages) overloaded IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service; the market-data farms broke and by 09:16 ET the IB Gateway's API port stopped accepting connections entirely, and IBC's RESTART could not revive it (its UI was wedged too). Only a container restart with a full login (phone 2FA) at 19:40 ET fixed it, so the whole session's option and index snapshots were lost with no backfill.

Both days show the same signature — option_snapshots and index_snapshots both failing at 09:10 with TimeoutError() after ~4 s, i.e. the IB Gateway's API port not accepting connections at that moment — but the runs alone do not show why the Gateway was unreachable, and the two days differ in what followed. On 2026-10-27 the 09:10 slot was the only failure of the day (81/82 option runs succeeded, 78/78 slots covered, SLI2 97.44%); on 2026-10-30 the same 09:10 failure occurred (78/78 slots covered, SLI2 100%) and the day also carried a 2103 farm code at 14:40. A 4-second connect timeout that clears by the next slot is consistent with a brief Gateway restart/login or a transient connectivity blip, not with the 2026-10-26 wedged-Gateway pattern (which produced failures every slot from 09:16 to the close). The data does not distinguish gateway_restarting from transient_reconnect, so the cause is not established.

A routine IBKR connectivity blip: the 1100 (connectivity lost) at 10:00 was followed by 1102 (restored, data maintained) at 10:05, and the 2103 farm drop was followed by 2110 (farm OK) in the same run. The session was never lost and no slot was missed: all 78 option slots on 2026-11-05 succeeded and the day's SLIs are met. No action needed.

Nothing is wrong with the Gateway. The 2157/2103 codes are routine, self-recovering IBKR data-farm blips: every option run that logged them still succeeded with full quote coverage, and no option run failed on 2026-11-11 (or 11-09). Runbook gateway section D says farm drops that recover within the same run are routine and not alerted; no action needed.

The IB Gateway's API was unreachable for about 15 minutes before the open on 2026-11-10: the 09:10, 09:15 and 09:25 option and index snapshot runs each failed their connect with TimeoutError() after ~4 s, and the 09:20 option run failed with ConnectionError('Socket disconnect' / 'Not connected') on every chain. The slots queued behind the failures then started late (09:25:15–09:26:03 instead of 09:10/09:15/09:20/09:25). Collection recovered by itself at the next slot, so this was a short Gateway/connectivity outage, not a wedged Gateway or a secdef stall. The data does not show whether the Gateway was restarting/logging in or the farms dropped: the failed runs carry no 1100/2103/2105/2157 codes, and no Gateway or Airflow logs are available here.

The data volume is full: every collector task fails immediately (2 s) with OSError(28, 'No space left on device') when writing raw output. The IB Gateway is healthy — the last runs before the failure succeeded with no IBKR error codes — so this is a host disk-space problem, not a market-data or connectivity problem.

The nightly dbt build could not take the write lock on data/curated.duckdb because another Python process (PID 4127) already holds a handle on it — per runbooks/duckdb-lock, even a read-only session (DuckDB CLI, notebook, DBeaver, Python REPL) blocks the build. Collection itself is unaffected: raw/staged Parquet is written by the collectors, not through DuckDB.

Every equity_bars run on 2026-11-12 was rejected by Alpaca with HTTP 401 Unauthorized (bad/expired API keys), so no bars were written all day; the 17:30 eod refetch of the last 10 sessions failed the same way. IBKR collection (option_snapshots, index_snapshots) is unaffected because it doesn't use Alpaca.

IBKR error 10197 ("live data held by another session of the same user") is being returned on every option and index snapshot run: the collector's IBKR user has a competing live session (TWS, mobile, web or a second Gateway), so the Gateway connects and the runs complete, but IBKR serves no live quotes — nearly every contract comes back with no_quote. This is a subscription/session problem (runbooks/gateway section C), not a Gateway fault: self-healing and RECONNECTDATA cannot fix it, and a restart would not either.

No runs were recorded at all for 2026-11-12 (or 2026-11-13): the scheduler/host produced nothing that day, so no option, index or equity data was collected and no Discord cards were sent. The data does not show why the host stopped — there are no failed runs, no IBKR error codes and no partial runs to point at a Gateway, subscription or vendor cause — so this is a host/scheduler outage (host_down) rather than a Gateway or data problem.

IBKR's contract-definition (secdef) service stalled on the morning of 2026-11-12: the 08:20 Gateway check's contract lookup (合约查询) got no answer within 20 s, and the pre-open option and index snapshot runs then hung on their first request until the 6-min run budget was used up. The Gateway itself stayed up (equity bars from Alpaca were unaffected all day, and the 15:xx option/index slots succeeded), so this is the secdef stall of runbooks/gateway section B, not a frozen or restarting Gateway.

Six consecutive option_snapshot slots (11:00–11:25) each ran exactly 480 s — the 8-minute execution timeout — and were killed with no error text recorded, while index snapshots and equity bars were unaffected. The data does not show which of the two runbook causes applies: a single hung IBKR request consuming the whole run budget (hung_request) or runs simply too slow for their budget (run_budget_exceeded). No error string, chain_errors, IBKR code or Gateway log is available for this window, so the cause cannot be pinned down from the tool results.

IBKR market-data farms were disconnected (codes 2103/2105) from 13:00 to 13:30 ET, so the SPX underlying had no spot price and every option-snapshot run in that window failed with "SPX: no spot price". The farms recovered on their own by the 13:30 slot; no Gateway restart or manual action was needed.

The IB Gateway was not logged in during 09:10–10:15: it was sitting in the IBKR two-factor login (2FA initiated 08:58, "Login has completed" only at 10:17), so the API port refused/timed out every connection. Each option and index snapshot run failed its connect in ~4 s with TimeoutError(); collection resumed on the first slot after the login completed. The data does not show why the Gateway was logging in at 08:58 (no 1100/2103/2157 codes, no secdef stall, no host-down catch-up burst in the runs), so the trigger of the re-login is not established.

Alpaca returned no bars for a window starting around 12:45 ET on 2026-11-12: every equity_bars run from then on succeeded but reported missing_bars=450 (50 symbols × 9 five-minute bars), and the 17:30 eod refetch of the last 10 sessions still reports missing_bars=450 for 2026-11-12, so the gap is not yet recovered. No run failed and there is no Alpaca error in pipeline_runs, so the cause is a vendor-side data gap rather than an API/auth failure; whether the eod refetch will fill it on a later pass is not yet shown by the data.

The 11:00 option_snapshots run hit a 300 s TimeoutError while the Gateway logged IBKR 1100 (connectivity lost) followed by 1102 (restored, data maintained) — a routine IBKR reconnect of the same session, not a Gateway outage. The failed run used its whole 5-min budget, and with max_active_runs=1 the following slots started late until the schedule caught up around 11:30. The data does not show a secdef stall, farm outage or Gateway freeze: index snapshots and equity bars kept succeeding and the Gateway stayed connected.
